title: Bolivian guerrilla campaign of Che Guevara
summary: In November 1966, Ernesto 'Che' Guevara arrived in Bolivia to establish the National Liberation Army (ELN), seeking to create a continental revolutionary focus using rural guerrilla foco doctrine. Operating in the rugged southeastern scrublands around Ñancahuazú, the insurgents faced isolation, lack of peasant recruitment, and internal estrangement from the Bolivian Communist Party. Surrounded by U.S.-trained Bolivian Rangers aided by CIA operatives, Guevara was captured in the Quebrada del Yuro on 8 October 1967 and executed the next day at La Higuera.

uncertainty.note: Guevara entered Bolivia in early November 1966; combat erupted in March 1967 and ended with his capture and execution on 8–9 October 1967.

as_recorded.value: entered Bolivia from Brazil on a Uruguayan passport in November 1966
executed in the hills of Bolivia after being captured by a U.S.-trained Bolivian military battalion

where.modern_name: La Higuera, Vallegrande Province, Santa Cruz Department, Bolivia

importance.justification: The defeat and execution of Che Guevara marked the definitive failure of the rural foco insurgency model in South America and solidified Guevara's iconographic legacy.
